anomalies.observed: On the schematic, the shared serial servo bus net labeled TTL is connected to U1 pin 6 (MAX3485 A). R15 (2.2k) connects this TTL/A node to GND. The B line (U1 pin 7) has R6 2k to +3V3 and R8 2.2k to GND, but the TTL/A line has no pull-up.
anomalies.expected: For the intended serial mode, J3 pin 3 and J8 pin 3 are tied to a shared TTL bus driven by the MAX3485 and controlled by the TXD2-based auto-direction circuit. A UART/RS-485 idle-high fail-safe requires the non-inverting A/TTL line to be pulled up toward +3V3 (or otherwise biased so A > B when idle), not pulled down to GND.

evidence.quote: Sheet /, right side: U1 MAX3485 pin 6 is labeled A and connects to the net labeled TTL; R15 2.2k connects that TTL/A node to GND. R13/R14 connect J3/J8 pin 3 to the TTL net.

Serial mode ... J3-pin3 and J8-pin3 are tied together into one shared bus node and driven by U1 (MAX3485), fed from the M5Stack's PortC UART (/TXD2//RXD2 ...) with Q2 auto-switching the transceiver's DE/RE pins based on TX activity.
R6, R7, R8, R15 2k, 20k, 2.2k, 2.2k Bias/pull network on the MAX3485 A/B differential lines and DE/RE enable line.

anomalies.impact: The shared servo TTL bus is held low when the transceiver driver is disabled. The MAX3485 receiver output will not see the normal UART idle-high state, RXD2 can be stuck low, and high bits on the bus cannot be produced by the pull-up/fail-safe network. Serial servo communication would fail or be unreliable.

parsed.summary: An anomaly is detected: the MAX3485/TTL serial bus appears to be pulled down to GND through R15 instead of being pulled up for idle-high UART/RS-485 fail-safe operation, which would prevent the intended shared serial servo bus from behaving correctly.
